name: Bullous Diffuse Cutaneous Mastocytosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Cutaneous Mastocytosis

criteria.description: Presence of widespread tense bullae on erythematous or normal skin
Histopathological demonstration of dense mast cell infiltrate in the dermis
Positive Darier's sign (urtication and erythema upon rubbing lesions)
Elevated serum tryptase levels above age-adjusted normal range
Detection of activating KIT gene mutations in lesional skin or blood

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (clinical bullae and histopathological mast cell infiltrate) or one major plus two minor criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology and laboratory findings; genetic testing may aid but is not mandatory.

imaging: Skeletal X-rays demonstrating osteopenia or lytic lesions
other: Positive Darier's sign on physical examination
Histopathology showing dense dermal mast cell infiltrate with toluidine blue or Giemsa stain

distinguishingFeatures: Bacterial culture positive for Staphylococcus aureus
Absence of mast cell infiltrate on biopsy
Genetic testing positive for collagen or keratin mutations
No mast cell proliferation or elevated tryptase
Direct immunofluorescence positive for linear IgA deposits
No systemic mast cell mediator symptoms

redFlags: Rapid progression of bullous lesions with systemic symptoms
Signs of anaphylaxis including hypotension and airway compromise
Development of hepatosplenomegaly or bone lesions indicating systemic involvement
references: Castells M. Mastocytosis: classification and clinical spectrum. Allergy Asthma Proc. 2015;36(3):177-184.
Valent P, Akin C, Metcalfe DD. Mastocytosis: 2016 updated WHO classification and novel emerging treatment concepts. Blood. 2017;129(11):1420-1427.
